alfriston.heading: ALFRISTON
alfriston.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, crisp, juicy, sugary, and briskly flavoured.
alfriston.quality: one of the largest and best culinary apples
alfriston.storage: It comes into use in the beginning of November and continues till April.
alfriston.note: Synonyms Lord Gwydyr's Newtown Pippin, Oldaker's New, Shepherd's Pippin, Shepherd's Seedling; raised by Shepherd at Uckfield, Sussex.

american-summer-pearmain.heading: AMERICAN SUMMER PEARMAIN
american-summer-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, very tender, rich, and pleasantly flavored.
american-summer-pearmain.quality: An excellent early apple, either for dessert or kitchen use.
american-summer-pearmain.storage: It is ripe in the end of August, and will keep till the end of September.
american-summer-pearmain.climate: The tree is a healthy grower, a prolific bearer, and succeeds well on light soils.

api-etoile.heading: API ETOILLE
api-etoile.storage: It ripens about the middle or end of September.
api-etoile.note: Synonyms Pomme Etoillee, Gelber Sternformiger Api, Sternapfel; a flattened five-angled star-shaped Api.

baxters-pearmain.heading: BAXTER'S PEARMAIN
baxters-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, firm, brisk, and sugary, and with an abundance of pleasantly acid juice.
baxters-pearmain.quality: An excellent apple, suitable either for culinary purposes, or the dessert
baxters-pearmain.storage: in use from November to March.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFFER
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh, white with a yellowish tinge, crisp and delicate, brisk, juicy, and sugary, and with a rich, vinous, and aromatic flavor.
edelborsdorfer.quality: A dessert apple of the first quality
edelborsdorfer.storage: in use from November to January.
edelborsdorfer.climate: The bloom is very hardy, and withstands the night frosts of spring better than most other varieties.
edelborsdorfer.note: Synonyms include Edel Winterborsdorfer, Reinette Batarde, Reinette d'Allemagne, Queen's Apple, Maschanzker. Cordus (1561) praised its 'sweet and generous flavor, and the pleasant perfume which it exhales'.

brabant-bellefleur.heading: BRABANT BELLEFLEUR
brabant-bellefleur.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, firm, crisp, and juicy, with a sugary, aromatic, and pleasantly sub-acid flavor.
brabant-bellefleur.quality: An excellent culinary apple of the finest quality
brabant-bellefleur.storage: in use from November to April.
brabant-bellefleur.note: Synonyms Brabansche Bellefleur, Glory of Flanders, Iron Apple, Kleine Brabanter Bellefleur.

cellini.heading: CELLINI
cellini.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, juicy, brisk, and pleasantly flavored.
cellini.quality: A culinary apple of the first quality
cellini.storage: in use during October and November.
cellini.note: Originated with Leonard Phillips of Vauxhall, probably from the Nonesuch.

dutch-mignonne.heading: DUTCH MIGNONNE
dutch-mignonne.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, very juicy, rich, sugary, and aromatic.
dutch-mignonne.quality: A very valuable and delicious dessert apple
dutch-mignonne.storage: in use from December to April.
dutch-mignonne.note: Synonyms Christ's Golden Reinette, Grosze oder doppelte Casseler Reinette (Diel), Paternoster Apfel, Stettin Pippin, Hollandische Goldreinette.

fenouillet-gris.heading: FENOUILLET GRIS
fenouillet-gris.flavour: Flesh, yellowish-white, tender, crisp, rich, sugary, and aromatic, partaking much of the flavor of Anise--hence the origin of one of the synonymes.
fenouillet-gris.quality: An excellent dessert apple, and when well ripened is considered of first-rate quality by those who are partial to its peculiar flavor.
fenouillet-gris.storage: It is in season from December to March, and at an advanced period becomes woolly.
fenouillet-gris.climate: It requires a rich soil and warm situation, and succeeds well as a dwarf on the paradise stock.
fenouillet-gris.note: Synonyms Fenouillet, Pomme d'Anis, Anis, Graue Fenchelapfel, Anisapfel, Winter Anisreinette. Caraway Russet is not given as a synonym.

foxwhelp.heading: FOX-WHELP
foxwhelp.flavour: The juice of this variety is extremely rich and saccharine, and enters in a greater or less proportion into the composition of many of the finest ciders in Herefordshire, to which it communicates both strength and flavor.
foxwhelp.quality: By Worlidge it was esteemed among the choice cider fruits.
foxwhelp.note: Specific gravity of the juice 1076 (1080 when small and shrivelled). One of the oldest cider apples, listed by Evelyn; Evelyn's source says Fox-Whelp cider of the Forest of Dean is not to be drunk till two or three years old. Hogg mentions no acidity or astringency.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, juicy, and though not highly flavored, is an excellent culinary apple.
gloria-mundi.storage: It is in use from October to Christmas.
gloria-mundi.note: Synonyms Monstrous Pippin, Baltimore, Glazenwood Gloria Mundi, American Mammoth, Ox Apple, Pomme Melon, Belle Dubois. Hogg's separate entry 'Pound' is a different (striped) apple.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, sugary, with an exceedingly rich and powerful aromatic flavor.
golden-harvey.quality: one of the richest and most excellent dessert apples
golden-harvey.storage: in use from December to May; but is very apt to shrivel if exposed to light and air as most russety apples are.
golden-harvey.note: Synonyms Brandy, Round Russet Harvey. Also one of the best cider apples; juice specific gravity 1085.

holland-pippin.heading: HOLLAND PIPPIN
holland-pippin.flavour: Flesh, yellowish-white, firm, tender, juicy, sugary, and briskly acid.
holland-pippin.quality: A valuable apple, of first-rate quality for culinary purposes
holland-pippin.storage: it is in use from November to March.
holland-pippin.note: Langley's Holland Pippin, native of the Holland district of Lincolnshire; Hogg says it is NOT the Kirton Pippin of Ray and Austen (he lists Kirton Pippin separately), contrary to our aka.

sweet-bough.heading: LARGE YELLOW BOUGH
sweet-bough.flavour: Flesh, white, very tender, crisp, and very juicy, with a rich, sweet, sprightly flavor.
sweet-bough.quality: A dessert apple of first-rate quality.
sweet-bough.storage: Ripe in the beginning of August.
sweet-bough.note: Synonyms Large Early Yellow Bough, Sweet Bough, Early Bough, Bough, Sweet Harvest.

lucombes-seedling.heading: LUCOMBE'S SEEDLING
lucombes-seedling.flavour: Flesh, white, firm, juicy, and pleasantly flavored.
lucombes-seedling.quality: A culinary apple of first-rate quality
lucombes-seedling.storage: in use from October to February.

maiden-blush.heading: MAIDEN'S BLUSH
maiden-blush.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, brisk, and pleasantly acid.
maiden-blush.quality: A very beautiful culinary apple, but not of first-rate quality.
maiden-blush.storage: It is in use during September and October.
maiden-blush.note: American; esteemed near Philadelphia and considered the best for drying.

manningtons-pearmain.heading: MANNINGTON'S PEARMAIN
manningtons-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, and very sugary; with a brisk and particularly rich flavor.
manningtons-pearmain.quality: This is one of the best and richest flavored of our dessert apples.
manningtons-pearmain.storage: it comes into use in October and November, and continues in good condition till March.
manningtons-pearmain.note: Cameron of Uckfield: 'if gathered too soon, it looses much of its fine richness and is very apt to shrivel'. Originated about 1770 at Uckfield; named by Thompson after specimens sent in 1847.

nanny.heading: NANNY
nanny.flavour: Flesh, yellow, rather soft and tender, juicy, sugary, and highly flavored.
nanny.quality: A dessert apple of excellent quality, and when in perfection, a first-rate fruit
nanny.storage: it is in use during October, but soon becomes meally.
nanny.note: Bears some resemblance in flavour to Ribston Pippin.

reinette-du-canada.heading: REINETTE DE CANADA
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh, yellowish-white, firm, juicy, brisk, and highly flavored.
reinette-du-canada.quality: An apple of first-rate quality, either for culinary or dessert use
reinette-du-canada.storage: it is in season from November to April.
reinette-du-canada.note: Synonyms include Reinette du Canada, Reinette de Canada Blanche, Grosse Reinette d'Angleterre, Portugal, St. Helena Russet, Canadian Reinette, Canada Reinette.

ortley.heading: WOOLMAN'S LONG
ortley.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, crisp, brittle, juicy, with a rich, brisk, and perfumed flavor.
ortley.quality: An excellent apple of first-rate quality, suitable either for culinary or dessert use
ortley.storage: it is in season from December to April.
ortley.note: Synonyms Ortley, Van Dyne; originated in New Jersey.

jersey-black.heading: BLACK AMERICAN
jersey-black.quality: A medium sized dessert apple, of second-rate quality
jersey-black.storage: in use during November and December.
jersey-black.note: One-line entry from the Horticultural Society catalogue: roundish, dark red. Black American is an aka of Jersey Black in our record, but Hogg gives no other synonym, so the identity is not certain.

detroit-red.heading: DETROIT
detroit-red.flavour: Flesh, white, (sometimes stained with red to the core in exposed specimens,) crisp, juicy, of agreeable sprightly sub-acid flavor.
detroit-red.note: Quoted from Downing. Synonyms Red Detroit, Black Detroit, Black Apple, Large Black, Crimson Pippin - bright crimson becoming blackish purple, which fits our record (aka Black Detroit, Crimson Pippin).

fallawater.heading: FALLAWATER
fallawater.flavour: possessing in some degree a Newtown Pippin flavor.
fallawater.quality: An American variety, of second-rate quality.
fallawater.storage: It is in use in January
fallawater.note: Short entry from the Horticultural Society catalogue; large, ovato-conical, green and brownish red.

harrison.heading: HARRISON
harrison.flavour: It is of medium size, and ovate shape, yellow color, rich flavor, and producing a high colored cider of great body.
harrison.quality: has long enjoyed the highest reputation as a cider fruit.
harrison.storage: The fruit is very free from rot, falls easily from the tree about the first of November, and keeps well.
harrison.note: Quoted from Downing; originated in Essex County, New Jersey. Ten bushels make a barrel of cider.

baumanns-reinette.heading: REINETTE BAUMANN
baumanns-reinette.quality: A small dessert apple, of second-rate quality
baumanns-reinette.storage: it is in use from December till March, and is not apt to shrivel.
baumanns-reinette.note: One-line entry from the Horticultural Society catalogue: oblate, red.

williams-favourite.heading: WILLIAMS'S FAVORITE
williams-favourite.flavour: Flesh, yellowish-white, and of a very mild and agreeable flavor.
williams-favourite.quality: A large and handsome dessert apple, worthy of a place in every garden.
williams-favourite.storage: ripens from the last of July to the first of September.
williams-favourite.note: Quoted from Downing; originated at Roxbury near Boston.
